name: Mangar
confidence_why: One first-hand description, checked against the source; 3 other works consulted do not discuss stress.
catalog_citation: Blench, Roger M. 2003. Why reconstructing comparative Ron is so problematic. In H. Ekkehard Wolff (ed.), Topics in Chadic Linguistics: Papers from the 1st Biennial International Colloquium on the Chadic Language Family (Leipzig, July 5-8, 2001), 21-42. Koeln: Ruediger Koeppe.
catalog_locator: sec. 3.3 'Tones', p. 28. Mangar as a distinct attested Ron lect: sec. 1 p. 21 and sec. 2.3 p. 25.
catalog_quote: All attested Ron languages have three level tones as well as combination tones and this can therefore be posited in Proto-Ron. Tones have significant grammatical functions as well as lexical –for example making plurals or deriving verbs from nouns. [p. 21] The usual languages listed for the group are Daffo-Butura, Bokkos, Monguna, Mangar, Sha, Mundat, Karfa, Richa, Fyer, Tambas. [p. 25] Although the sources treat Mangar and Monguna as dialects of Daffo-Butura, and Tambas as very close to Fyer, the data hardly supports this. In the following analysis, all Ron lects are treated as distinct

new_statements.rule_in_words: Mangar, like every attested Ron lect, is a tone language with three level tones plus contour (combination) tones carrying lexical and grammatical load; the source says nothing about word stress or accent.
new_statements.exceptions: None; the statement is group-level (all attested Ron lects, Mangar included), not a Mangar-specific analysis.
new_statements.domain_note: Lexical/grammatical tone on words; no statement about stress at word or phrase level. Comparative paper based on Seibert's and Blench's field wordlists, not a phonological description of Mangar.
new_statements.identity_note: The only first-hand prosodic statement is a group-level one in Blench 2003 covering 'all attested Ron languages', among which Mangar is explicitly treated as a distinct lect (p. 21, p. 25). Older sources (Jungraithmayr 1970, Seibert 1998, Blench Atlas 2019/2020 index) count Mangar as a dialect of Daffo-Butura Ron (ronn1241); Glottolog 5.1 gives Mangar its own languoid mang1417 with no ISO code. Location per Blench Atlas ed. IV: Plateau State, Mangu LGA.
